title: TCP & UDP
description: Handshakes, reliability, flow control and when to pick UDP.

questions.prompt: Which sequence of segments sets up a TCP connection?
questions.explanation: The client sends SYN, the server answers SYN-ACK, and the client confirms with ACK. Both sides have then agreed on initial sequence numbers.

image.alt: A client and a server exchanging three numbered messages whose flags are not shown.

questions.prompt: Why might a team choose UDP over TCP for a live voice call?
choices: Low latency matters more than retransmitting every lost packet
questions.explanation: A retransmitted voice packet arrives too late to be useful. UDP avoids connection setup, retransmission and head-of-line blocking, and lets the application decide how to conceal loss.

questions.prompt: Which of these does TCP provide that plain UDP does not? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: TCP gives ordering, reliability and flow control. Both TCP and UDP use port numbers to multiplex applications.

questions.prompt: Which mechanism stops a fast TCP sender from overwhelming a slow receiver?
questions.explanation: Flow control uses the receive window the receiver advertises. cwnd is a sender-side limit that reacts to network congestion, which is a different problem.

questions.prompt: During TCP slow start, how does the congestion window typically grow?
choices: Linearly, by one segment per RTT
It shrinks until the first loss
questions.explanation: Slow start increases cwnd by one segment per ACK, which doubles it each round trip, until it reaches a threshold or sees loss. Congestion avoidance then grows it linearly.

questions.prompt: Which TCP flag is used to close a connection gracefully?
questions.explanation: FIN says 'I have no more data to send'. RST aborts a connection immediately, for example when a port is closed.

questions.prompt: Why does the side that closes a TCP connection first linger in TIME_WAIT?
choices: To wait for the application to flush its buffers
To make sure the final ACK arrives and old duplicate segments expire
To reserve the port for the next client
questions.explanation: TIME_WAIT (about 2×MSL) lets the last ACK be retransmitted if lost and prevents delayed segments from a previous connection being mistaken for a new one on the same 4-tuple.

questions.prompt: Which transport protocol does HTTP/3 run on?
questions.explanation: HTTP/3 uses QUIC, which is built on UDP and adds its own reliability, congestion control and TLS 1.3. This removes TCP head-of-line blocking between streams.
